question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=xy-{y}^{2}-1 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+5\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the behavior of the system’s solutions near the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}={[2,\text{ }1]}^{T}?$

$\,$
The equilibrium is an  
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}xy-{y}^{2}-1 \\ -{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+5\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $\text{\boldsymbol}f(x).$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-{y}^{2}-1)=y \\ \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-{y}^{2}-1)=x-2y \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+5)=-2x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+5)=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have:

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x-2y \\ -2x & -2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}(1) & 2-2(1) \\ -2(2) & -2(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), so the system is almost linear at ${x}^{∗}.$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 \\ -4 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(-2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=-2,1.$

Finally, since we have two real eigenvalues with opposite signs, our equilibrium is an $\text{unstable}$ $\text{saddle}.$
